scope.description: Four in-process nodes at protocol version 3 with 300ms heartbeat/election/lease: A and B bootstrapped as voters {A,B}; A snapshots, adds E as a caught-up nonvoter, adds C as a voter, commits four commands. A is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true so its configuration comes from the snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds {A,B,C}; B is partitioned; A issues AddVoter E, which the stale base turns into the two-server change {A,B,E} and which commits on A plus E. The probe then issues one client command on A (committed with A and E) and finally heals the partition, observing the entry at the created index and the FSM contents of A and of the old-majority leader.
assumptions: E is a caught-up nonvoter before the change, so {A,B,E} commits with A and E alone once B is partitioned.
The client command is an ordinary Apply on the leader that has a quorum of the configuration recorded in its own log ({A,B,E}: A and E).
MockFSM records one entry per LogCommand applied, so its length is the number of committed commands that node's FSM has consumed.
Both sides keep running the protocol; the partition is applied by disconnecting in-memory transports in both directions.
excluded: No control variant: with the flag disabled the configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create the disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration).
Leader concurrency is not asserted as a comparison here because its window depends on when the higher-term vote requests reach the stale leader.

basis.prefix: Real bootstrap, real snapshot, real AddNonvoter catch-up, real AddVoter, real commits, graceful shutdown and restart of the leader on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances, real client Apply, real transport partition and real healing. Nothing is fabricated.

comparisons.description: An entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs must not be replaced after the partition heals.
After a client write returns success on the leader, every node that follows the same log must apply the same committed commands; the FSMs of A and of the old-majority leader must not differ.

before.description: Four in-process nodes at protocol version 3 with 300ms heartbeat/election/lease: A and B are bootstrapped as voters {A,B}; A snapshots, adds E as a caught-up nonvoter, adds C as a voter (config {A,B,C} plus nonvoter E), commits four commands. A is shut down and restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true so its in-memory configuration comes from the snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry; the other three nodes get longer timeouts so the restarted leader wins back leadership. B is then partitioned from A (C is already absent from A's stale configuration, so A replicates to nobody but E), and A issues one AddVoter E. Observations: whether that change commits and with whose acknowledgement, each side's configuration and log tail, who leads each side and in which term, and the content of A's log at the created entry index before and after the partition is healed.
assumptions: E is a caught-up nonvoter before the change, which is what lets the silently-created {A,B,E} configuration commit with A and E alone once B is partitioned; this is ordinary use of AddNonvoter followed by AddVoter.
Restarting the leader with RestoreCommittedLogs=true is the documented configuration already established by the earlier receipts; nothing else about the cluster changes.
The partition is applied by disconnecting the in-memory transports in both directions, which is a real partition for all Raft traffic (AppendEntries, heartbeats, votes).
Both sides keep following the protocol: A leads the {A,B,E} configuration with E's acknowledgements, and B and C campaign under their own {A,B,C} configuration after their election timeout.
excluded: No control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter adds a single server and the two-server change cannot arise; that is a source-level statement (nextConfiguration over the current configuration) rather than an execution.
No disk faults or message loss; the only partition is the one applied explicitly.

prefix.before: Real bootstrap, real snapshot, real AddNonvoter catch-up, real AddVoter, real commits, graceful shutdown and restart of the leader on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances, real transport partition and real healing. The log, snapshot metadata and configurations all come from those operations; the harness never fabricates entries or configuration state.

before.description: An entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs must not be replaced after the partition heals.
At most one leader may exist for a given log: the old-configuration side must not elect a leader while the new-configuration side still leads.

after.description: An entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs must not be replaced after the partition heals.
After a client write returns success on the leader, every node that follows the same log must apply the same committed commands; the FSMs of A and of the old-majority leader must not differ.

revision_reason: The executed revision established the silent change and the truncation of the committed entry. This revision adds the client-facing observation of the same path: a client write issued on the {A,B,E} leader A after the silent change (committed with A and E) and the FSM contents of A and of the old-majority leader afterwards. It also drops the earlier 'at most one leader' comparison because a construction-time run of this revision observed A stepping down before the old side's leader was sampled (vote requests in the higher term reach A from the connected side), so the leader-concurrency window is schedule-dependent and is retained as an observation from the two scored executions rather than as a comparison in this harness.
